offence_severity: Life imprisonment for Section 302 IPC, five years' rigorous imprisonment for Section 354 IPC, and three years rigorous imprisonment for Section 201 IPC
physical_harm: The deceased sustained bleeding injuries on her head and ear, along with abrasions and swelling, leading to cardio-respiratory arrest due to head injuries.
number_of_offences: The accused was prosecuted for offences under Sections 364, 302, and 201 IPC. The courts upheld all the charges.
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the motive for murder was established through evidence of a wage dispute.
motive: The motive for murder was the wage dispute between the appellant and PW-1, who had abused the appellant at the village.
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of the doctor who conducted the post-mortem proved that the death was homicidal. The blood stains found on the appellant's shirt, considered along with the factum of the appellant having led the prosecution to discover his blood-stained clothes and the body of the deceased, could have been only that of the deceased.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of PW-3 (the mother of the deceased) and PW-7 (the shop owner) as reliable witnesses. The court also noted that the conduct of the child witness, who did not speak in court, was not found fault with and was held in favour of the prosecution.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 03.12.2000; Trial judgment: 10.02.2006; High Court decision: 10.02.2006; Supreme Court decision: 25.07.2013
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: P.C. Aggarwala, Revathy Raghavan; Counsel for the State: Sachin J. Patil, Sanjay V. Kharde, Asha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence confirmed; High Court: Conviction and sentence confirmed; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was last seen with the accused, there was an extra-judicial confession from the accused, blood-stained shirt of the accused was recovered, the dead body was found at the instance of the accused, and there was motive for murder.
defence_argument: The accused contended that there were doubts as to whether the death was homicidal and that the blood group of the accused was not tested to ascertain whether the blood stain on his shirt could be of his own blood.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the chain of circumstances against the accused was complete and that the death was homicidal based on the evidence of the post-mortem report.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the overwhelming evidence proving all the circumstances against the accused, including the homicidal nature of the death, the last seen theory, the blood-stained shirt, the recovery of the body, and the motive for murder.
